properties.name: Finding the cause of a failure is a process reflow2 serves, not one an agent improvises while under pressure to ship a fix
properties.statement:
When something has failed and somebody is about to fix it, the steps of root cause analysis SHALL be delivered as a procedure the agent executes, not as advice it may recall — and the procedure SHALL be reachable at the moment of the work rather than read once at the start of a session.

It SHALL require candidate causes to be GENERATED FROM THE DESIGN rather than recalled, because "think of three causes" yields two real ones and a filler that exists to satisfy the instruction. Where the project has an implementation, the artifact layer SHALL be the path from a symptom to the source files that could have produced it.

It SHALL require, before any fix is proposed, a measurement that could REFUTE the leading candidate. A measurement that merely confirms it is not evidence: almost any observation is consistent with a plausible cause, which is what makes it plausible.

Where the design cannot answer, it SHALL say so rather than fall silent — an unmodelled file, an undeclared seam and an unwritten requirement all look identical to a graph that has never been told about them, and that silence must not read as the absence of a cause.

Driven by Anthony, 2026-08-28: "quite a few cases now where in using reflow2 on a project, the agent proposes a solution to an issue, then goes off and implements some solution, but it turns out that the solution only treated a symptom or superficial issue and not the root cause."
